title: What inherits, and what does not
summary: Text properties flow down to children; box properties do not. inherit forces it.
explanation: The panel sets a colour, a font, a border and padding. The paragraph inside picks up the colour and the font (text properties inherit) but gets no border or padding of its own (box properties do not).
Some elements block inheritance with their own browser styles: the link keeps its blue and the button keeps its system font. color: inherit and font: inherit hand them the parent's values instead.
The keyword inherit works on any property, even ones that do not normally inherit: border: inherit on .boxed copies the panel's border.
tryThis: Delete color: inherit from .panel a: the link goes back to browser blue.
Delete font: inherit from .panel button: the button switches to the system font.
Remove the .boxed rule: the last paragraph loses its border, because border never inherits on its own.
